candidates.statement: Checkout p95 latency is elevated (~437ms) while all sampled checkout requests return 200. Traces show the order path dominated by downstream calls: POST order spans ~92ms with payment authorization ~23ms and postgres save_order ~15ms, and inventory reservation ~2.5ms. Latency concentrates in downstream service calls rather than gateway errors.
candidates.uncertainty: No per-dependency latency metrics or logs; cannot isolate which downstream (order/payment/postgres) dominates the tail.

report.explanation: All observed checkout requests return 200 with no 502s, so http-500 and db-pool-exhaustion are unsupported (pool size/idle=1, no wait). Redis reserve_inventory is fast (~2.5ms), arguing against redis-timeout. Memory retained is well under limit with no retention history, so memory-leak is unsupported. Elevated checkout p95 with downstream-dominated spans best fits downstream-latency, though localization needs more evidence.
missing_evidence: Per-dependency latency histograms for order, payment, inventory, postgres to localize the tail
Gateway logs (excluded) to confirm no errors or timeouts
Baseline checkout p95 to confirm the 437ms is anomalous
